key: Through all this world strode Visnu; thrice his foot he planted, and the whole Was gathered in his footstep’s dust.
s: Near the close of a hymn calling a round of gods to the rite, six verses turn to Visnu and his strides; Sāyaṇa, on 1.22.17, reads it of Visnu in his descent as Trivikrama, the three-strider, whose dusty footprint held the whole visible world.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.22.17, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 352131 (2022)

opened.locator: translation of 1.22.17 and notes on 1.22.15 to 1.22.17

evidence.words: विष्णुः त्रिविक्रमावतारधारी “इदं प्रतीयमानं सर्वं जगदुद्दिश्य "वि “चक्रमे विशेषेण क्रमणं कृतवान् । तदा “त्रेधा त्रिभिः प्रकारैः “पदं “नि “दधे स्वकीयं पादं प्रक्षिप्तवान् । “अस्य विष्णोः “पांसुरे धूलियुक्ते पादस्थाने “समूळ्हम् इदं सर्वं जगत् सम्यगन्तर्भूतम्।
evidence.gloss: Vishnu, bearing the Trivikrama descent (avatāra), strode in a special striding over this whole world that appears to us. Then he set down his foot in three ways. In the dusty place of this Vishnu’s foot this whole world was completely contained.

reason: The problem holds: the key verse and the neighbouring verses 1.22.16 to 1.22.20 in day.js print Griffith’s ‘Visnu’, and day 20 writes ‘Visnu’; the sentence wrote ‘Vishnu’ twice. Changed both to ‘Visnu’ and nothing else.
